sources.note: Para 84 'Stress' p. 475 is a Papuan-Tip-Cluster-wide remark, not Galeya-specific: 'In all of the languages of PTC it seems that stress is predictable within certain word-classes, notably kinship nouns and verbs. When a kinship noun is pluralised by the addition of a suffix, the stress moves one syllable closer to the end of the word..'; Dobu has penultimate vowel lengthening; stress phonemic in Kilivila, Muyuw, Budibud, Misima. Galeya appears only in para 46 (location/dialects, p. 459) and para 81 (labialised glottal stop, p. 474).

sources.citation: Lambrecht, Philip, Alison Kassell & Margaret Potter. 2015. The Sociolinguistic Situation of the Galeya Language Group. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2015-022. Dallas: SIL International. 98 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Appendix D 'Characteristics of the language: Phonology' (pp. 69-70) gives phone charts, CV syllable structure, glottal-stop variation and final-vowel syncope only; the 170-item IPA wordlists (Appendix I, 7 Galeya-dialect villages + Dobu) carry no stress marks. Names Engkvist & Troolin 2002 (unpublished SIL-PNG ms) as the only other work charting Galeya phonology/grammar.
